summary: Feed s132_double is degraded: 98.5% encrypted traffic exceeds NDR 90% tolerance and VLAN 20 is missing (50% untagged) due to tag stripping, severely limiting payload inspection and VLAN-aware detection.

findings.root_cause: 98.5% of bytes are encrypted (TLS) and forwarded without decryption. Packet broker is delivering encrypted payloads directly to the NDR, exceeding its 90% encrypted-share tolerance. No SSL/TLS visibility/decryption stage is configured before the tool.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs full payload for DPI, JA3, and behavioral detection. With payloads opaque, detection is reduced to flow metadata only; C2, exfiltration, and lateral movement signatures that require payload will be missed.

recommended_fix.why: Decrypt or selectively forward decrypted traffic (e.g., via TLS visibility appliance / broker decryption) to bring encrypted share below 90% so NDR can inspect payloads as required.

findings.root_cause: Required VLAN 20 not seen; 50% of packets arrive untagged. Upstream TAP/SPAN or packet broker is stripping 802.1Q tags on ingress/egress, so VLAN context is lost before delivery to the NDR.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requires VLANs 10 and 20 for segmentation and correlation. Without VLAN 20 tags it cannot apply VLAN-aware policies or detect east-west threats per segment, creating blind spots and incomplete coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker and TAP/SPAN to preserve and forward 802.1Q tags for VLANs 10 and 20 end-to-end so NDR receives correctly tagged traffic for full coverage.
